title: Ground that spans the world: one heightmap terrain with layers, grass and rocks standing on it, in Rust
note: Hills, valleys and beaches are one Terrain made in on_reset from a pure height function, painted by layers, grassed, and drawn with frame.terrain.
intent: Ground across the world is one heightmap Terrain made once in on_reset, never a field of cubes. Terrain::from_fn([samples, samples], origin, spacing, height) takes a pure height function (genex::math for sin and cos, no world, no clock), or Terrain::from_heights(samples, origin, spacing, &heights) row-major. .with_layers(vec![..]) sets up to 16 layers, TerrainLayer::textured(albedo, data, tile) or TerrainLayer::flat(color); .with_control(&texels) paints one TerrainTexel::blend(base, overlay, amount) per height sample. A grassy layer gets .with_grass(Grass::meadow(density, height)); paint that layer near the grass's colour: low presets draw the ground alone. Draw it every frame with frame.terrain(&ground): one draw that never pops or cracks. terrain.height(x, z) puts the player and things on the ground, the same bits everywhere. Rocks and bushes come from terrain.scatter(&Scatter::new(density, &layers).on_flat_ground(0.9), min, max) once, kept as an InstanceGroup drawn with frame.group. Refusals (terrain-heights-invalid, terrain-layers-invalid, terrain-control-invalid) change nothing. A frame draws one terrain; a world past about a kilometre streams (rust.streamed-world).
port: The world's owner makes and draws the terrain; another facet places its things with terrain.height and never draws a second ground.

evidence.note: Terrain::from_fn or from_heights, layers and a control texel per sample, grass on a layer, terrain.height, terrain.scatter and the three refusals.
A height function uses genex::math, so the ground and everything placed on it are the same bits on every destination.
Scattered rocks are made once and drawn as one group with frame.group.
